answers.question: List of scenarios
answers.evidence: "We chose three Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) scenarios as a means of testing and challenging the resilience of our business model across a range of plausible climate futures: • Outpatient scenario reflects emissions reduction and decarbonisation occurring at a manageable, non-critical state and relates to SSP1... • Emergency Department scenario reflects emissions reduction and decarbonisation needing critical attention and relates to SSP2... • High Dependency Unit scenario reflects a deteriorating state of the environment and climate and relates to SSP3."
answers.notes: The company gave each SSP scenario a custom medical-themed name: Outpatient (SSP1), Emergency Department (SSP2), High Dependency Unit (SSP3).

answers.question: Global temperature outcome by 2100
answers.answer: Three temperature outcomes are described: 1.5°C (Outpatient/SSP1 — peaks at 1.5°C by 2050, settling to 1.4°C in 2100); 2.7°C (Emergency Department/SSP2 — by 2100); 3.6°C (High Dependency Unit/SSP3 — by 2100). No temperature overshoot is explicitly described beyond the SSP1 peak-and-decline note.
answers.evidence: "1.5°C Global temperature increase peaks at 1.5°C by the year 2050, before settling to 1.4°C in 2100." / "2.7°C Global temperature increase by the year 2100." / "3.6°C Global temperature increase in 2100."
answers.notes: The SSP1 scenario notes a peak of 1.5°C by 2050 then a slight decline to 1.4°C by 2100, which could be interpreted as a mild overshoot, though the document does not use the word "overshoot".

answers.question: Customised scenarios
answers.evidence: "As a medical device and technology company with an extensive global footprint (deriving 99% of revenue outside of New Zealand), we did not consider that there was a suitable sector-wide scenario analysis to draw upon. We developed our own climate scenarios for the analysis... We prepared scenario narratives to provide a compelling illustration of how different temperature outcomes and pathways would affect our strategy and business model in plausible future states."
answers.notes: The company explicitly states it developed its own scenarios because no suitable sector-wide scenario existed. It used SSP frameworks as a base but customised them with proprietary healthcare market demand modelling, company-specific physical risk mapping of owned/leased sites, and bespoke scenario narratives tailored to its medical device business model. The scenarios were also given custom names (Outpatient, Emergency Department, High Dependency Unit).
answers.ani_notes: Yes, Using insights from our proprietary healthcare modelling and insights from global population data, we estimated patient cohort size and associated medical capacity required for a range of respiratory conditions in each scenario.
